title: CCPA & California Privacy Security Checklist
metaDescription: Complete CCPA compliance checklist for California residents and businesses. Protect your privacy rights with our step-by-step guide.
intro: The California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) and its enhancement, the CPRA, give California residents powerful privacy rights. This checklist helps you understand and exercise these rights while ensuring businesses stay compliant with California's privacy laws.

items.task: Learn what personal information businesses collect about you
items.why: CCPA gives you the right to know what data is collected, used, shared or sold about you by businesses.
items.howTo: Review privacy policies of services you use. Look for 'California Privacy Rights' sections that detail data collection practices and your rights under CCPA.

items.task: Understand the differences between CCPA and CPRA
items.why: CPRA expands CCPA with stronger protections, including sensitive personal information categories and correction rights.
items.howTo: CPRA added rights to correct inaccurate data, limit use of sensitive info, and created the California Privacy Protection Agency for enforcement.

items.task: Identify what qualifies as sensitive personal information
items.why: Under CPRA, you have additional rights over sensitive data like health info, precise location, and biometrics.
items.howTo: Sensitive data includes SSN, driver's license, financial accounts, precise geolocation, racial origin, religious beliefs, union membership, and biometric identifiers.

items.task: Verify if businesses you interact with fall under CCPA
items.why: Only businesses meeting certain thresholds (revenue over $25M, handle 50K+ consumers, or earn 50%+ from selling data) must comply.
items.howTo: Large retailers, social media platforms, and data brokers typically qualify. Check their privacy policies for CCPA compliance statements.

items.why: Some data types like publicly available information and certain business contexts have exemptions from CCPA requirements.
items.howTo: CCPA doesn't apply to public records, deidentified data, or employee data (with some exceptions). Review specific exemptions in each company's privacy policy.

items.task: Submit 'Do Not Sell My Personal Information' requests
items.why: This prevents businesses from selling your personal data to third parties for monetary or other valuable consideration.
items.howTo: Look for 'Do Not Sell My Info' links on websites (usually in footers). Submit requests via web forms, email, or phone. No account creation should be required.

items.task: Limit use and disclosure of sensitive personal information
items.why: Under CPRA, you can restrict how businesses use your sensitive data beyond what's necessary for basic services.
items.howTo: Look for 'Limit the Use of My Sensitive Personal Information' links or contact businesses directly. This right applies to data like health info and precise location.

items.task: Request access to your personal information
items.why: You have the right to know what personal information businesses have collected about you in the past 12 months.
items.howTo: Submit data access requests through company privacy portals or contact forms. Businesses must respond within 45 days with categories and specific pieces of data collected.

items.task: Request deletion of your personal information
items.why: You can ask businesses to delete personal information they've collected about you, with some exceptions for operational needs.
items.howTo: Use company deletion request forms or contact customer service. Verify your identity as requested. Note that some data may be retained for legal or security reasons.

items.task: Request correction of inaccurate personal information
items.why: Under CPRA, you can ask businesses to fix incorrect personal information they maintain about you.
items.howTo: Contact businesses directly with specific corrections needed. Provide documentation supporting the corrections when possible. This is a new right under CPRA.

items.why: Private browsers help prevent data collection and tracking that feeds into the data ecosystem covered by CCPA.
items.howTo: Use Incognito Browser or similar privacy tools that block trackers by default. Enable 'Do Not Track' signals and regularly clear cookies and browsing data.

items.task: Update privacy policies with CCPA-required disclosures
items.why: CCPA mandates specific privacy policy content including data categories, sources, business purposes, and third-party sharing details.
items.howTo: Include sections on consumer rights, data categories collected, retention periods, and contact information for privacy requests. Update annually or when practices change.

items.task: Create systems to handle consumer privacy requests
items.why: Businesses must provide at least two methods for consumers to submit requests and respond within required timeframes.
items.howTo: Set up web forms, dedicated email addresses, and toll-free numbers. Train staff on verification procedures and 45-day response requirements (extendable to 90 days).

items.task: Add required 'Do Not Sell' links to your website
items.why: If you sell personal information, you must provide a clear 'Do Not Sell My Personal Information' link on your homepage.
items.howTo: Place the link prominently in your website footer and ensure it leads to a simple opt-out mechanism that doesn't require account creation.

items.task: Train employees on CCPA compliance procedures
items.why: Staff handling consumer requests must understand verification requirements, response timeframes, and proper handling of privacy rights.
items.howTo: Develop training materials covering request types, identity verification, data location procedures, and escalation processes. Update training for CPRA changes.

items.why: CCPA requires opt-in consent before selling information of consumers under 16, with additional protections for those under 13.
items.howTo: Implement age verification mechanisms and parental consent processes. Maintain records of consent and provide easy withdrawal methods.

items.task: Conduct regular privacy audits and risk assessments
items.why: Regular audits help ensure ongoing compliance and identify areas where privacy practices may need updates.
items.howTo: Review data flows, third-party contracts, retention policies, and security measures. Document compliance efforts and address any gaps identified.

pro_tips: Set calendar reminders to review and update your privacy settings quarterly, as companies often change their data practices.
Keep records of all privacy requests you submit, including screenshots and confirmation emails, in case you need to follow up or file complaints.
Use the California Attorney General's website to stay updated on CCPA enforcement actions and new guidance that might affect your rights.
Consider using a privacy-focused browser like Incognito Browser by default to minimize data collection before it even begins.
If you're a business, consider working with privacy management platforms that can automate much of the CCPA compliance process and reduce manual workload.
